title: Chapter 1126
paragraphs: Chapter 1126
Episode 258. The Predator of All Dimensions (16)
Gurgle, kuuuuuk...!
Kelliark's desire was churning. Now, no matter where one looked on the battlefield, there were no elements to recognize that this place had once been the Black Sea.
Only a viscous, red desire churned like a great sea. For now, there was still enough high ground to stand on, but it seemed that soon even that would be buried.
It was a sight no one had ever seen before. Even Kelliark himself had never thought his desire would materialize in such a way.
Only Helluram had foreseen it. That if Kelliark succeeded in shedding his skin one more time, such a phenomenon would probably occur.
His desire would fill the entire world, and all life and objects would be trapped within it and suffocate.
Helluram too had wanted such an end. But not in the form of this unpleasant desire, but in a form filled with darkness and the abyss.
Tzzaaaak...!

The center of the red sea of desire was opening like a mouth. Within it was a dimensional gate unlike any that had appeared on the battlefield before, and from within, an elongated stone was seen rising.
The Origin Stone.
The first to be completed by Kelliark in the 33rd dimension, an abomination the likes of which would never be seen again in the world.
"It's certainly damaged..."

Kelliark clicked his tongue and grabbed the Origin Stone with both hands. The surface that should have been hard was soft like a rotten mushroom, and the authority of manipulation and distortion that should have been transmitted just by touching it felt only faint.
"But you should have destroyed it completely, Helluram. So that I couldn't even think of fixing it."
Plop! Kelliark threw the Origin Stone into the flowing red sea as if releasing a caught fish.
This desire was, after all, a part of, or the entirety of, Kelliark Zipple. To him, it was no different from putting it in his pocket.

"It will take some time, so until then, let's enjoy the rest of the fight, everyone. As you can see... thanks to you all, I have crossed a certain line that even I didn't know existed. I have become something that never was before, and never will be again."
"Yes... a little while ago, you were at least wearing human skin, but now I don't know what to call you."
At Jin's words, Kelliark nodded his head.

"I am still wearing the skin. Well, what would be good to call me? The incarnation of desire? The absolute? Such things are cliché. But even if it's cliché, I don't think there's a more accurate word to describe me."
The One True God.
Kelliark grinned.

"Among the immortals that have existed in the world until now, no. Beyond that, even the being who created the world did not possess an authority superior to mine. And I don't even have to worry about self-destructing in agony like Kinzelo. To contemplate whether to maintain, destroy, or reconstruct the world... it doesn't suit me, does it?"
If it's lacking, fill it. If it's useless, remove it. If it's not to my liking, make it so.
Kelliark continued his words and even whistled. The signs of fatigue from being cornered had vanished without a trace.
He was just standing there defenselessly, but no one dared to attack.
It was because they had to block Kelliark's desire from flooding their inner selves. All the Coalition members, including the Genesis Knights, and even Helluram.
The Demon Army, which had been losing faith, was bowing to Kelliark.
"I have doubted you, my lord."
"It is true that I intended to rely on you, Midor. You, along with the Vamel Alliance, are the last humans to have given me a sense of caution."
"What shall I do?"
"I still need you all. So continue to fight. Until the Origin Stone regains its form. I won't need you after that, but that doesn't matter anymore, does it?"
"Of course.
As soon as Midor answered, he felt his body relax. It was because Kelliark had momentarily released them from the wave of desire.
"This is the Demon Army's final battle. Let's end it with a victory."
Their magic hadn't become stronger than before, nor had their combat power suddenly increased. Rondo's group was still exhausted.
But the Coalition had to fight while continuously suppressing the impulse Kelliark was creating. Their minds were dull, and their bodies were bound to be slow.
"Keok!"

The first to be pierced by the magic of Rondo's group was Touven. He stood there with a hole in his chest larger than his head and met his death, and before his comrades could call his name, his body turned entirely to ash and scattered.
The golden fleet couldn't pressure the enemies as heavily as before, and Murakan, the only Genesis Knight on the central front, was experiencing the most severe impulse among all of the Coalition.
[This isn't real, damn it... It's not!]
Murakan was already muttering to himself as if he had half-lost his mind.
Instead of the reality of the war with the Demon Army, the red sea, the dying comrades, and Kelliark Zipple, he was seeing an illusion created by the impulse.
The impulse Murakan was experiencing, Kelliark's desire.
What Kelliark intended to do as the one true god was like the creation that the Sun God Kinzelo had performed at the beginning of time. Shaping the world, giving rise to life.
In other words, the creation Kelliark desired was to make 'the world he wanted'.
That was why Murakan was now seeing the world he had dreamed of instead of reality.
A world where Temar Zipple doesn't die, a world where Solderet doesn't disappear.

A world where he doesn't have to kill the ghostly Pray, Iolo, and Dranax with his own hands, a world where he wakes up from a thousand-year-long sleep and doesn't have to lose his comrades again like this.

The red sea was drawing everyone on the battlefield to be swept up in such impulses, to see illusions. It was just that Murakan was the first to start breaking down; it seemed that eventually, everyone would become like him.

"You desire, and I correct your desires. When the Origin Stone is restored, Murakan will now see something different. He will see an illusion of trampling the things he loved with his own hands for the sake of Zipple. He will sincerely come to want that to happen. And that illusion will become reality."
No one can know what their true desire is. Everything is tuned and corrected by Kelliark's desire.
"This is the method I have decided upon to rule the world as the one true god, Jin Runcandel."
"Murakan!"

Beams of magic and space explosions fired by Rondo's group covered Murakan. Murakan, lost in his illusion, could not dodge. If his comrades and the golden fleet hadn't put up a shield for him, one of the beams would have pierced his heart.
[Ugh... ugh.]
"Murakan, get a grip!"
Though he was shouting, Jin too was barely pushing back the creeping impulse.

Of course, the world he wanted to achieve through his regression was not like this. He hadn't wanted to change the fate of so many people, nor had he wanted to bring his loved ones into such a terrible fight.

'I must be calm. Murakan has lost his mind, but the rest can still fight. The curse removal... assuming there are no problems. Then we just have to hold out for one more hour. To endure for one hour against the mental manipulation he's causing...'
He needed Valeria.

The answer was only Valeria. She had to find the records. She had to find the record stating that they were being subjected to Kelliark's mental manipulation and continuously show it to their comrades.
"Valeria."
No answer came.
With a chilling feeling, Jin quickly turned his head to look at her.
"Valeri... ah."

Valeria was staring down at the crimson seawater that had risen up to her waist, her expression vacant. The recording window floating in front of her had stopped updating after the last sentence, 'The desire of Kelliark Zipple spreads'.
She too, like Murakan, was already trapped in an illusion.
In the days she lived with the Gray Owl Mercenaries, in the moment she walked along the beach of Honka Island with Jin, on the last night she spent with Jin.
Those memories were the few moments of happiness in Valeria's life.

They were also a misfortune. She was endlessly wandering through the illusion, searching for a world where happiness could remain as only happiness until the end. She was already tired beyond what she could bear.
"Unfortunately, it seems Valeria Hister has decided to rest now too, Jin Runcandel. What will you do now? What else will you do to surprise me..."
[Jin Runcandel.]
Helluram cut off Kelliark's words and called Jin's name.
[One hour. I will hold Kelliark Zipple. You all find Solderet's final legacy.]
The Witch Helluram.

Even if she helped the Coalition to stop Kelliark, she had intended to prevent Jin from entering the legacy at all costs. From the beginning, Helluram, Malugia, and the Coalition had ultimately pursued different goals.
But now, Helluram had no other choice either. For her, it was simply choosing the lesser of two evils, not the worst.
"Witch Helluram, it seems the immortal of the old era still has some strength left."

[You're excited like a child, orphan. The Origin Stone has not yet been restored. The status of the one true god is not yet yours. Whether there is one minute left until the restoration is complete, or ten minutes. Until then, it is not.]
As if to mock those words, as Kelliark extended his hand, Malugia and Araxion came out of Helluram's embrace. They were motionless, like stopped machines.
"To have the final piece for absorbing the Sun God's power taken away so easily, you're full of confidence. Why don't you try saying it like before? That you have a plan for everything."
In the center of the battlefield, his comrades were still struggling to protect the unconscious Murakan.
[Murakan, wake up! If you're gone, we all die.]
The Genesis Knights of the battlefield were gathering around Jin. For now, they had no choice but to hope that Helluram would keep her word.
Jin held Valeria and looked out at the vast, desolate red sea.

The Authority of Regeneration, which had shone so brilliantly, was buried in desire and not even a speck could be seen, and now Jin had to search this entire sea to find the entrance to the sanctuary again. He had to wait for the curse on Temar's left arm to be lifted, even one second faster.
[Wipe that look off your face, you bastard... hook. Anyone would think it's all over.]
It was Orgal.
[It's desperate, but you're the first one to come this far. That alone is hope. Somehow, until the very end, let's grab that damn bastard and pull him down.]
No path was visible anywhere in the red sea. It was daunting, but it was a familiar task.
